title: Using Substring to replace CopyStr
summary: BC 27.1 and later resolve a runtime error when using the Substring method with length parameters that exceed string boundaries, making it safe to replace CopyStr with Substring for improved code readability.
key_points: Substring caused runtime errors in BC versions before 27.0 platform builds when the length parameter exceeded the available string length
BC 27.0 online includes the fix but BC 27.0 on-premises does not; BC 27.1 is the first application version with the fix across all deployments
CopyStr remains supported with no plans for obsolescence; both methods can coexist
Set the application property to 27.1.0.0 or higher in app.json to safely use Substring; the runtime property does not affect this fix

quotes.text: With BC 27.1 and beyond, you can safely replace CopyStr with Substring to improve code readability!
quotes.why_it_matters: This signals when developers can confidently migrate to the newer, more readable method.

quotes.text: Index and length must refer to a location within the string.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is the exact error message developers encountered when using Substring with invalid length parameters in earlier versions.

quotes.text: BC 27.1 is the first application version having the fix in any case.
quotes.why_it_matters: This clarifies the minimum version requirement for guaranteed Substring support across all deployment types.
